Existing exact COUNT and whole-match sorting explain work beyond 200 rows; it is not N+1 or deep pagination. No new regression or agreed SLO violation was established; no optimization or new merge blocker was introduced.

bounded_remaining_scope.detail: D-011 withdrawal is implemented and tested. The wider title also includes taxes, reversals and financial retention; those operating-policy decisions are not established by approving withdrawal state transitions. Existing integer-money/order/refund tests remain reusable, not new proof of tax or real-settlement policy.

The new lifecycle portion has current multi-layer evidence. Full querying/filtering, create/bulk-generate, edit/ban/key/inviter, mail and export evidence needs business-point mapping from existing CI/packaged/Oracle results; do not rerun all flows merely to unify metadata commits or claim intercepted UI writes were persisted.

Current evidence is SQLite v63 lifecycle, exact 30-day boundaries, explicit anonymization, authority, rollback, credential revocation, owned-notification fencing and retained business facts. Browser proves deactivate/recover; final anonymization is exercised at API/store and component levels. Unknown historical mail ownership and already-started network sends retain the documented limits. Formal acceptance stays pending.

D-013 offline 90-day metadata preservation, fact reconciliation, fixed replay and rollback are verified. No historical-query UI was requested by D-013. Actual off-site restore and production database/token-transition decisions are separate; representative synthetic migration is not a production migration rehearsal.

The captured real snapshot identified by SHA-256 aebf5ecea99ec21056c7f9a0e25bad33657e347d was not available in the inspected test locations. Synthetic adapter, migration and plugin UI tests are not a substitute for this opt-in snapshot identity test.

Proprietary Stash, Surge, Shadowrocket, Quantumult X, Loon and Surfboard real-import execution is unavailable. Pinned Mihomo and sing-box CI results cover only their actual binaries and formats, not those proprietary products.

Supported-browser/accessibility scope, real third-party sandbox endpoints and visual compatibility sign-off remain explicit choices. No extra UI or third-party production calls were added during closeout.

Production database compatibility, legacy-token retirement, SLO/capacity, cutover/rollback, administrator MFA, real off-site recovery and independent production authorization are not released by this development candidate.
